exposure: pre-gravid underweight body mass index (BMI <18.5 kg/m2)
cohort: 10,995 pre-gravid underweight mothers and 146,155 pre-gravid normal weight mothers
finding: Pre-gravid underweight mothers had a higher incidence of preterm birth and low birth weight infants, but a lower incidence of cesarean births, gestational diabetes, and hypertensive disorders compared to normal weight mothers.
mod_finding: Lean mothers had a significantly lower incidence of cesarean births.
birth_weight: low and very low birth weight
